subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap-only hook scheduling as the bounded fix for the linked bootstrap-context stall, despite possible prompt-order and session-timing differences for existing extra-bootstrap configurations?
rationale: The patch is technically strong and well-proven, but it changes compatibility-sensitive prompt assembly and scheduling behavior; automation cannot choose whether that runtime tradeoff is acceptable.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Validation
options.body: Accept the bounded compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, run focused parity and exact-head gates, then merge.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but require a current-head embedded-run or connected-channel transcript demonstrating responsive I/O during bootstrap before merging.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Do not land this branch if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching over a custom bootstrap-path walker.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Validation
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded compatibility tradeoff, rebase onto current main, run focused parity and exact-head gates, then merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history spans all three decision surfaces: internal hooks, bootstrap hook integration, and guarded workspace reads.
